newsitem.title: SPAIN: Aznar to meet Clinton, aims to raise Spain profile.
newsitem.headline: Aznar to meet Clinton, aims to raise Spain profile.

text.p: Spain's Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar makes his first official visit to the United States next week, likely to win praise for his government's hard line against Cuba and its growing role in NATO.

Aznar, a former tax inspector whose centre-right government came to power almost a year ago, will hold talks with U.S. President Bill Clinton at a time when Spain is trying to raise its international profile.

Spanish officials said the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) would be the main focus of Wednesday's White House meeting. Madrid is hosting a landmark summit in July expected to open the door to a major NATO expansion.

"Spain is keen to play a more prominent role in the reformed NATO, but it has given up its bargaining chip by agreeing to enter NATO's military structure, so it will be keen to garner U.S. support," said a source close to Aznar's administration.

Spain decided last year to integrate fully into NATO's military structure. The choice of Madrid for the NATO summit was seen as a reward for Spanish cooperation while France continues to hold off on full integration.

Also likely to figure prominently in next week's talks is Cuba, a former Spanish colony. Clinton is expected to give Aznar a pat on the back for taking a stronger stance against the communist-ruled island.

Aznar's Popular Party government, the first right-wing administration in Spain since the dictatorship of Francisco Franco ended in 1975, has reversed the softer Cuba policy of his Socialist predecessors and urged the European Union to do the same.

"Aznar wants reassurance from the Americans on Cuba and he wants to be told that they are grateful for what he is doing, especially as an advocate of American policy in the EU," a political analyst said.
"But at the same time Aznar doesn't want to be perceived in Spain as being a poodle (to Clinton)," he added.
Tension between Spain and Cuba rose last year when Havana accepted and then withdrew approval for a new Spanish ambassador, accusing Spain of interfering in its internal affairs.
Aznar, who leaves for the United States on Sunday and returns on Friday, is travelling with Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato and Foreign Minister Abel Matutes.

Before heading to Washington, the prime minister flies to New York, where on Monday he will meet United Nations Secretary General Kofi Annan and explain Spain's wish to increase its presence in U.N. agencies.
The U.S. visit will be a chance for Aznar, who has won praise for his economic policies, to step up his effort to claim a place for Spain in the first tier of European powers.

"Aznar is not the world's most charismatic player: he doesn't speak foreign languages, he's generally perceived as being slightly provincial and not a high flier, so this trip will be aimed at raising his image, especially as a European statesman," one analyst said.
Aznar will take advantage of his stay in New York to meet big players at the New York Stock Exchange to discuss investment opportunities in Spain.
In Washington, he will be especially eager to push his role as the key man in Europe-Latin America relations.
"The Spanish government wants the U.S. to acknowledge Spain as the key player in EU-Latin American relations rather than France and that is a goal that is well within reach now," said one analyst.
In Washington Aznar will also see Vice President Al Gore, Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin, Justice Secretary Janet Reno and Defence Secretary William Cohen.
